initiative.title: Autonomous Execution Integrity
initiative.summary: Make goal scope, session ownership, automation retries, and integration provenance hard runtime invariants so parallel agents cannot absorb, repeat, or silently expand each other's work.

taskset.summary: Freeze goal-run membership, isolate every writer session, move live coordination out of source history, make effects idempotent, and prove serialized integration under concurrency and failure.

tasks.title: Freeze goal-run scope and require attested transitions
tasks.goal: Turn a conversational goal into an immutable execution contract whose exact taskset, task, and unit membership cannot grow during the run.
tasks.scope: Add the GoalRun and ScopeChangeRequest model on the canonical runtime-state store, deterministic membership hashing, and planner-facing start/status/amend/close commands. Preserve existing work records and provide an explicit compatibility path for raw goal text.
acceptance: Starting a goal seals exact taskset, task, and unit IDs plus relevant hashes and base SHA.
Work registered after sealing is reported as discovered-after-scope and is never executable in the current run.
Scope amendment requires an approval reference, records old and new digests, and increments a monotonic revision.
The completion predicate is evaluated only against frozen membership.
The registration path can express dependencies between locally created tasks without guessing future task IDs.
A newly registered dynamic taskset is immediately resolvable by taskset and wave dispatch.

units.title: Implement immutable GoalRun storage and membership hashing
units.context: The current loop stores only raw goal text while wave dispatch resolves the live taskset on every invocation. A run needs a durable identity and sealed membership before any writer claim is created.
units.scope: Define GoalRun, immutable membership snapshots, deterministic digests, base SHA, budgets, completion predicates, and atomic local persistence. Do not wire dispatch or session leases in this unit.
steps: Write failure-first tests for task and unit additions after scope sealing.
Define versioned GoalRun and ScopeChangeRequest schemas.
Resolve exact membership and hash normalized work-item identity and unit-spec inputs.
Persist start, status, and close transitions through the canonical runtime-state adapter.
Document compatibility behavior for a raw goal that has no sealed run.
acceptance: The same inputs produce the same membership digest.
A live registry addition does not change an existing run record.
Corrupt or partially written state fails closed.
Run identity is independent from human-readable goal text.
units.handoff: Provide the GoalRun schema, persistence location, digest fixtures, and before/after proof that a newly added unit is excluded.
units.stop_condition: Stop before changing dispatch, claim acquisition, or Git behavior.

units.title: Add explicit scope amendment and registration dependency aliases
units.context: Conversation follow-ups must remain flexible without silently becoming execution authority. The current registration path also cannot reference another task created in the same input without guessing its future numeric ID.
units.scope: Add start/status/amend/close command surfaces, proposal-only discovery intake, approval attestations, and registration-local dependency aliases. Do not authorize automatic scope growth.
steps: Classify follow-ups as context, constraint, scope expansion, replacement, or separate goal.
Write a pending ScopeChangeRequest for membership changes.
Require an owner approval reference before creating the next revision.
Resolve registration-local task aliases after numeric IDs are reserved.
Make a work.py-registered taskset immediately resolvable through the dynamic taskset registry.
Add CLI and template parity tests.
acceptance: A newly discovered task becomes a planning proposal, not runnable work.
A boolean approval flag without attestation cannot amend scope.
Old scope revisions remain immutable and auditable.
A single registration file can declare an internal unit dependency DAG without preselected task IDs.
wave_dispatcher --taskset resolves a newly registered dynamic taskset without a static code entry.
units.handoff: Demonstrate rejected implicit expansion, approved revision creation, and stable dependency alias resolution.
units.stop_condition: Stop before modifying wave dispatch or claim validation.

tasks.title: Bind dispatch, loops, and supervision to a frozen run
tasks.goal: Ensure every selection, claim, restart, and completion decision uses one exact goal run and scope revision rather than live backlog or raw goal text.
tasks.scope: Make wave dispatch consume sealed membership, make claims validate the same digest, and make agent_loop and goal_supervisor resume only an exact run. Do not implement the session lease store in this task.
acceptance: Wave planning for a goal selects only IDs sealed in its active scope revision.
A claim outside the sealed scope fails before persistence.
Agent loops consume only run-bound work and never drain an unrelated role inbox.
Supervisor restarts identify an exact run and reject a mismatched scope digest.
Frozen completion stops even when new backlog exists.
verification: python -m pytest -q tests/test_wave_dispatcher.py tests/test_task_claim_dispatcher.py tests/test_agent_loop.py tests/test_goal_supervisor.py tests/test_taskset_boundary_gate.py

units.title: Select and claim only frozen goal-run members
units.context: wave_dispatcher currently re-enumerates every current unit in a taskset. The taskset boundary gate is repository-global and only activates after completion.
units.scope: Add run and scope-revision inputs, select manifest IDs instead of live taskset membership, and validate scope digest before claim creation. Do not add session fencing yet.
steps: Reproduce a unit added after scope sealing entering the next wave.
Plan from the sealed unit list and classify later units as discovered-after-scope.
Require run ID, revision, and digest on mutating claims.
Key boundary decisions by run and session rather than every repository claim.
Add template parity coverage.
acceptance: Later work never enters the frozen wave.
Unrelated goal runs cannot block each other's boundary checks.
A stale or mismatched digest fails closed before a claim file or event exists.
units.handoff: Attach the late-unit and cross-goal regressions plus the manifest-based wave plan.
units.stop_condition: Stop before moving runtime state storage or changing Git operations.

units.title: Resume the exact run and stop on frozen completion
units.context: agent_loop carries a raw string and goal_supervisor finds the latest goal in a shared daily log. Concurrent sessions can therefore resume the wrong work or continue into generic inbox messages.
units.scope: Bind loop start, dispatch, stop events, restart counts, and completion to run ID and scope revision. Preserve a read-only compatibility report for legacy raw-goal events.
steps: Write two-session fixtures with identical goal text and different run IDs.
Pass exact run identity through loop events and dispatch.
Remove generic inbox consumption from run-bound execution.
Resume only if run identity, revision, digest, and lease status still match.
Stop at frozen completion and report later discoveries separately.
acceptance: Identical goal text cannot cross-resume another run.
Restart counters are per run rather than per text.
New backlog after completion does not re-arm the completed run.
units.handoff: Show two same-text runs remaining isolated across stop and restart.
units.stop_condition: Stop before implementing durable effect idempotency or session SCM enforcement.

tasks.title: Make session and claim ownership atomic and durable
tasks.goal: Give each writer one exclusive session, worktree, branch, and fenced claim lease without advancing a source branch.
tasks.scope: Build a canonical local control-plane store under the Git common directory, issue monotonic fencing tokens, make claim acquisition transactional, remove live-state autocommit, and preserve read-only projections for operators.
acceptance: Two simultaneous acquisitions for one task, worktree, branch, or semantic domain produce exactly one winner.
Every writer lease includes session, run, worktree realpath, branch, base SHA, generation, fencing token, and expiry.
Claim creation and heartbeats do not change Git HEAD or status.
A stale token cannot mutate or release a newer lease.
Existing tracked claim history can be read and migrated without fabricating ownership.
verification: python -m pytest -q tests/test_runtime_state_store.py tests/test_claim_lease.py tests/test_task_claim_dispatcher.py tests/test_parallel_worktree_gate.py tests/test_multi_host_claim_gate.py

units.title: Build the canonical control-plane store and fenced lease primitive
units.context: Claim conflict checks and persistence are separate operations, and tracked worktrees hold divergent snapshots of active claims. A local canonical store must serialize acquisition across linked worktrees.
units.scope: Implement a Git-common-dir SQLite WAL or equivalently locked transactional adapter with unique live-owner constraints and fencing generation. Define an adapter contract for a future multi-host CAS backend.
steps: Write concurrent-process acquisition and crash fixtures.
Define versioned session, goal, claim, heartbeat, and projection tables.
Enforce unique active ownership for task, worktree realpath, branch, and declared semantic domain.
Increment fencing generation on every reacquisition.
Expose read-only status and recovery diagnostics.
acceptance: Concurrent acquisition has one committed winner.
Expired ownership can be recovered only with a higher fencing token.
Partial writes and process death preserve a consistent store.
The store is shared by linked worktrees but absent from product Git history.
units.handoff: Provide transaction traces for simultaneous acquisition, stale-token rejection, and crash recovery.
units.stop_condition: Stop before changing worker Git command authorization.

units.title: Move live claims out of source history and project compatibility views
units.context: Claim autocommit protects against reset/clean by creating the cross-session source commits that later sessions treat as unknown work.
units.scope: Persist live coordination in the control-plane store, disable source-branch claim autocommits, and generate compatibility summaries only through a serialized projection owner. Preserve immutable released evidence where policy requires it.
steps: Assert that create, heartbeat, and release leave HEAD and status unchanged.
Persist claim lifecycle with session/run identity and fencing.
Replace tracked live claim reads with canonical store reads.
Provide explicit migration for legacy tracked claims.
Make one projection actor responsible for optional tracked summaries.
acceptance: A worker claim cannot create a source commit.
All linked worktrees read the same active ownership state.
Legacy evidence remains available without being treated as a live lease.
Worker branches contain product/work-item changes only.
verification: python -m pytest -q tests/test_task_claim_dispatcher.py tests/test_claim_guard.py tests/test_agent_instance_registry.py tests/test_parallel_worktree_gate.py
units.handoff: Show unchanged HEAD/status around a complete claim lifecycle and consistent status from two linked worktrees.
units.stop_condition: Stop before deleting historical claim records or broad repository cleanup.

tasks.title: Enforce session-owned SCM and quarantine foreign state
tasks.goal: Prevent a writer from staging, committing, pulling, merging, pushing, reverting, or closing over work owned by another session.
tasks.scope: Add a session SCM guard, exact-path staging, commit provenance, branch/ref ownership, foreign-state classification, and session-local dirty/closure behavior. Integration authority remains a separate role.
acceptance: One mutating session owns exactly one worktree and branch.
Worker Git operations are restricted to owned paths, commits, and the claimed remote ref.
Broad staging and worker pull/merge/rebase/cherry-pick are blocked.
Sibling worktree or branch progress is classified as foreign observation and does not block closeout.
Unexpected changes inside the owned worktree fail with attributable ownership evidence.
verification: python -m pytest -q tests/test_session_scm_guard.py tests/test_agent_loop.py tests/test_stop_hook_session_scope.py tests/test_session_baseline.py tests/test_dirty_intake.py tests/test_closure_gate.py

units.title: Guard every worker mutation and remove broad staging
units.context: agent_loop checkpoint uses git add -A, and current claim metadata cannot prove that a commit or push belongs to one session.
units.scope: Validate cwd, real worktree, exact branch, lease token, staged paths, commit trailers, and push ref before every worker mutation. Do not implement merge-queue integration in this unit.
steps: Create negative fixtures for git add -A, commit -a, pull, merge, rebase, cherry-pick, and foreign ref push.
Replace checkpoint broad staging with the session-owned actual delta.
Require session, run, claim, and unit provenance trailers.
Allow only HEAD to the exact claimed remote branch with expected-old-SHA protection.
Revalidate the fencing token in hooks, pre-commit, and pre-push.
acceptance: No broad staging command remains in worker recovery paths.
A worker cannot mutate a sibling or protected branch.
Stale lease generation fails at every mutation boundary.
A valid owned commit and push still work.
verification: python -m pytest -q tests/test_session_scm_guard.py tests/test_agent_loop.py tests/test_claim_guard.py tests/test_safe_ref_op.py
units.handoff: Provide the allowed/blocked Git command matrix and exact-path checkpoint evidence.
units.stop_condition: Stop before granting worker access to merge or integrate sibling commits.

units.title: Make dirty, stop, and closeout decisions session-local
units.context: The current Stop helper infers touched paths from transcripts and repo-wide gates see every claim, branch, and worktree. This turns valid sibling work into a recurring unknown-change bottleneck.
units.scope: Compute owned change from manifest plus base-to-HEAD and worktree delta, classify foreign state, and restrict closeout obligations to the current session. Do not hide unattributed edits in the owned worktree.
steps: Record session, run, claim, worktree, branch, base, and initial HEAD in the baseline.
Classify owned, expected-generated, foreign-observed, overlap, external-base-progress, and unattributed changes.
Make sibling state informational unless it overlaps an owned path or semantic domain.
Route attributable foreign findings to the owner session instead of halting the observer.
Keep unattributed owned-worktree edits blocking.
acceptance: Two dirty sibling worktrees can close independently.
origin/main advancement is external base progress, not an unknown local edit.
A sibling-only commit never enters this session's closeout set.
A true same-worktree intrusion still blocks with owner/claim detail.
verification: python -m pytest -q tests/test_session_baseline.py tests/test_stop_hook_session_scope.py tests/test_dirty_intake.py tests/test_closure_gate.py tests/test_parallel_worktree_gate.py
units.handoff: Show the classification matrix and a two-session closeout regression with no reciprocal blocking.
units.stop_condition: Stop if the implementation would downgrade unattributed edits in the current owned worktree.

tasks.title: Make footprints, semantic domains, and dependencies mandatory
tasks.goal: Prevent duplicate or incompatible parallel work before dispatch, including overlaps that do not share exact file paths.
tasks.scope: Fail closed on empty and escaped actual footprints, acquire semantic-domain ownership atomically, enforce dependencies globally, and keep generated/shared surfaces under a single projection owner.
acceptance: Mutating claims without target files and semantic domains cannot start.
Actual diff outside the claimed footprint blocks release and integration.
Two claims for the same semantic domain cannot coexist even when target paths differ.
Dependencies are checked across all active and completed work, not only one taskset view.
Generated shared views are modified only by their designated projection owner.
verification: python -m pytest -q tests/test_footprint_conflict_gate.py tests/test_task_claim_dispatcher.py tests/test_task_unit_readiness_gate.py tests/test_wave_dispatcher.py tests/test_state_sync_gate.py

units.title: Enforce planned and actual ownership across files and domains
units.context: Empty target_files currently warn, file footprints miss semantic conflicts, and isolated taskset views can overlook global dependency state.
units.scope: Require explicit file and semantic footprints, validate actual diffs at release/integration, and resolve dependencies against canonical global state. Preserve read-only/research exemptions with explicit claim mode.
steps: Turn footprint-less mutating claims from warning to blocking.
Add normalized semantic-domain declarations and atomic acquisition.
Compute actual base-to-HEAD and dirty footprints and reject escape.
Resolve dependency completion from canonical work and claim state.
Reserve generated shared surfaces for the projection owner.
acceptance: Read-only work can run without a write footprint only when explicitly classified read-only.
A semantic collision is detected before either worker writes.
Release cannot pass when actual files exceed the lease.
A dependency completed in another taskset is recognized without importing its branch.
verification: python -m pytest -q tests/test_footprint_conflict_gate.py tests/test_task_claim_dispatcher.py tests/test_task_unit_readiness_gate.py tests/test_wave_dispatcher.py tests/test_state_sync_gate.py
units.handoff: Provide path, domain, generated-surface, and global-dependency conflict fixtures.
units.stop_condition: Stop before changing protected remote branch policy.

tasks.title: Make automation loops durable and idempotent
tasks.goal: Prevent process restarts, retries, and duplicate dispatch from repeating steps or externally visible effects.
tasks.scope: Add a durable run-step-attempt ledger, idempotency keys, effect receipts, global retry budgets, progress checks, cancellation propagation, and compensation pointers. Keep provider-specific effects behind adapters.
acceptance: A run step has a stable idempotency key across restart.
A completed effect with a receipt is reconciled rather than repeated.
Retry limits apply across process restarts with backoff, jitter, and circuit breaking.
No-progress repetition halts with a classified reason.
Cancelling a goal run prevents child dispatch and queued effects from continuing.
verification: python -m pytest -q tests/test_run_step_ledger.py tests/test_agent_loop.py tests/test_goal_supervisor.py tests/test_stop_events.py src/agent_runtime/templates/project/scripts/test_auto_dispatch.py

units.title: Persist run steps, effect receipts, retries, and cancellation
units.context: Current iteration and failure caps are per process. Supervisor restart can repeat a logical step because there is no durable cursor or effect receipt.
units.scope: Persist intent, lease, attempt, receipt, result, retry, cancellation, and compensation metadata for logical steps. Do not directly implement provider-specific irreversible actions.
steps: Define idempotency as run ID, scope revision, and logical step ID.
Write intent before an effect and reconcile a receipt before retry.
Track attempt, time, cost, and token budgets across processes.
Add exponential backoff with jitter and no-progress detection.
Cascade cancellation to children and queued effects.
acceptance: Crash-after-effect-before-result does not repeat the effect when a receipt exists.
Concurrent duplicate dispatch elects one step lease owner.
Retry exhaustion is durable and cannot reset with a new process.
Non-reversible effects carry an explicit recovery or compensation pointer.
verification: python -m pytest -q tests/test_run_step_ledger.py tests/test_agent_loop.py tests/test_goal_supervisor.py tests/test_stop_events.py src/agent_runtime/templates/project/scripts/test_auto_dispatch.py
units.handoff: Attach crash-window, duplicate-dispatch, retry-budget, no-progress, and cancellation traces.
units.stop_condition: Stop before enabling any new external side effect by default.

tasks.title: Seal integration with SHA-bound remote attestation
tasks.goal: Make the serialized integration authority the only path that can absorb worker commits into the protected branch.
tasks.scope: Verify commit provenance, revalidate against the current base, bind gate results to exact SHAs and gate versions, and enforce required remote checks and protected gate policy.
acceptance: Only the integration role may merge, rebase, cherry-pick, or advance the protected branch.
Every candidate commit belongs to one released session/claim and valid scope revision.
Gate evidence is bound to repository, base SHA, candidate SHA, task, run, and gate bundle.
Remote required checks cannot be satisfied by evidence for a different SHA.
Candidate changes to gate policy are evaluated under protected-base policy and elevated review.
verification: python -m pytest -q tests/test_merge_queue.py tests/test_merge_queue_policy.py tests/test_session_scm_guard.py tests/test_remote_gate_attestation.py tests/test_gate_governance.py

units.title: Require provenance and exact-SHA attestation in the merge queue
units.context: A strong local queue remains bypassable when remote branch policy is permissive or when an attestation is not cryptographically tied to the exact candidate and base.
units.scope: Add integration-role authorization, commit-chain provenance, latest-base revalidation, exact-SHA attestation, and protected gate governance. Do not weaken existing local checks.
steps: Reject candidates with foreign, unattributed, or stale-fence commits.
Revalidate dependency, scope, lease release, and actual footprint at queue time.
Seal gate input and output to base SHA, candidate SHA, run, task, and gate bundle version.
Configure required remote check consumption and expected-old-SHA protected update.
Use protected-base policy when the candidate modifies a gate or baseline.
acceptance: A passing attestation cannot be replayed for another commit.
A candidate whose HEAD changes during verification is rejected.
Direct worker integration is denied.
Gate self-weakening cannot authorize itself.
verification: python -m pytest -q tests/test_merge_queue.py tests/test_merge_queue_policy.py tests/test_remote_gate_attestation.py tests/test_gate_governance.py
units.handoff: Provide attestation schema, replay/tamper fixtures, branch-policy evidence, and a protected update trace.
units.stop_condition: Stop before modifying a live remote policy without explicit owner authorization.

tasks.title: Strengthen semantic verification and baseline governance
tasks.goal: Prevent mechanically green integration from restoring old designs, mixing incompatible implementations, or laundering regressions into new baselines.
tasks.scope: Add contract, journey, responsive, accessibility, visual, and verifier-attestation requirements plus independent ownership for baseline and gate changes.
acceptance: Critical user journeys have semantic assertions independent of snapshots.
Design-system ownership and shared component contracts are checked across parallel branches.
Baseline updates require separate justification, before/after evidence, and non-author independence.
Verifier identity and tool evidence are bound to the candidate SHA.
A green unit suite cannot override a failed journey, accessibility, or protected design contract.

units.title: Add semantic integration and independent baseline controls
units.context: Bean Wiki demonstrated that ordinary CI can remain green while navigation, design, or responsive behavior regresses after parallel integration.
units.scope: Define repository-configurable critical journeys, design contracts, responsive/accessibility evidence, verifier provenance, and protected baseline approval. Do not encode one product's UI into core defaults.
steps: Define semantic assertions that cannot be replaced by snapshots.
Bind journey and verifier evidence to the candidate SHA.
Require independent approval and rationale for baseline updates.
Detect incompatible ownership of shared design contracts.
Integrate blocking results into the merge attestation.
acceptance: Known green-but-wrong fixtures fail.
Baseline changes cannot self-approve.
Non-UI repositories can configure equivalent domain contracts without visual tooling.
Verifier evidence names actor, tools, inputs, and exact commit.
units.handoff: Provide a green-unit/red-journey fixture, baseline-approval matrix, and exact-SHA verifier evidence.
units.stop_condition: Stop before globally requiring a product-specific browser or screenshot stack.

tasks.title: Prove concurrent-session safety and roll out enforcement
tasks.goal: Demonstrate that the current reciprocal-blocking and duplicate-work chain cannot recur across crashes, races, retries, and incompatible parallel changes.
tasks.scope: Build end-to-end concurrency and failure-injection scenarios, migrate existing state, run shadow mode, define observability and rollback, then enable hard enforcement by measured stages.
acceptance: The pre-fix unknown-change chain is reproduced deterministically and fails after remediation.
Race, crash, stale token, retry, cancellation, late task, foreign state, and semantic conflict scenarios pass.
Legacy tracked live state migrates without losing audit evidence or creating active ownership.
Shadow-mode metrics quantify false positives and bypasses before blocking rollout.
Rollback preserves source history, run state, and ownership integrity.
verification: python -m pytest -q tests/test_parallel_session_isolation.py tests/test_bounded_goal_scope.py tests/test_runtime_chaos.py tests/test_control_plane_migration.py tests/test_enforcement_rollout.py

units.title: Run chaos scenarios, migrate state, and stage enforcement
units.context: The safety model spans scope, leases, Git, loops, integration, and verification. Unit tests alone cannot prove the absence of reciprocal blocking or duplicated effects.
units.scope: Exercise real concurrent processes and temporary linked worktrees, migrate legacy coordination state, and define shadow-to-block rollout with telemetry and rollback. Do not enable blocking in consumer repositories until exit criteria pass.
steps: Reproduce reciprocal unknown-change blocking and duplicate claim/effect races.
Inject process death at lease, effect, verification, and protected-update boundaries.
Test late registration, sibling dirt, base advancement, stale fencing, and incompatible design domains.
Migrate legacy tracked state as historical evidence rather than active ownership.
Run observe, warn, block-new, and block-all stages with explicit exit and rollback criteria.
acceptance: A clean session closes while an unrelated sibling worktree is dirty.
Only one simultaneous same-scope claimant or step executor succeeds.
A late task never enters a sealed run.
Crash recovery neither duplicates effects nor accepts stale writes.
Rollout metrics and recovery runbook are sufficient for an operator to reverse enforcement safely.
verification: python -m pytest -q tests/test_parallel_session_isolation.py tests/test_bounded_goal_scope.py tests/test_runtime_chaos.py tests/test_control_plane_migration.py tests/test_enforcement_rollout.py
units.handoff: Attach the chaos matrix, pre/post failure traces, migration report, shadow metrics, and staged rollout decision.
units.stop_condition: Stop before broad hard enforcement if any P0 race, false-positive ownership block, or rollback data-loss case remains.
